//: Typecheck config for the PURE-MODULE unit tests. HAND-WRITTEN AND COMMITTED.
RUNS ON A STOCK RUNNER (AD-23). It deliberately does NOT widen to `gi://*`
or `ags/*`: nothing reachable from here may import GTK, which is what keeps
the suite runnable with no AGS and no GTK4 installed. The desktop-stack
typecheck is the separate tsconfig.platform.json.
WHY THE EXPLICIT `.ts` SUFFIX (resolves the spine Open Question). Node runs
these files natively via its built-in TypeScript type-stripping, and Node's
ESM resolver does NOT do extensionless lookup, so `from "../ports/event-client"`
would fail at RUNTIME. The suffix is load-bearing. `allowImportingTsExtensions`
is what lets tsc agree with Node.
WHY RELATIVE, NOT THE `ags-platform` BARE SPECIFIER. Node rejects `.ts` under
`node_modules` (`ERR_UNSUPPORTED_NODE_MODULES_TYPE_STRIPPING`), so the test
runner cannot import the package by name through a `node_modules` shortcut.
Relative imports exercise the same source files with no build step and no
desktop stack; AGS's embedded esbuild (not Node) resolves the bare specifier
for real apps.
`types: ["node"]` is a DECLARED dependency for `node:test`/`node:assert`.
`make typecheck-tests` installs @types/node at the repo root (npm install
--no-save, gitignored); tsc's typeRoots walk from tests/ finds
node_modules/@types/node one level up.
